query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a thin, uniform Al2O3 coating on as‐cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr via atomic layer deposition (ALD) will inhibit oxygen ingress at high temperatures and thereby improve its oxidation resistance without compromising its room‐temperature ductility or high‐temperature yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy that exhibits 8–16% room‐temperature tensile ductility and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C (strain rates 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹) but suffers from rapid internal oxidation due to poor oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Apply a thin (approximately 100–200 nm) aluminum oxide (Al2O3) coating using atomic layer deposition (ALD) on the alloy’s surface.
generation.conditions: Expose both coated and uncoated alloy samples to high-temperature air (approximately 1000 °C) for an extended duration (e.g., 100 hours) under mechanical loading conditions similar to those used in previous tests (strain rates 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹).
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, adherent, and defect‐free Al2O3 layer that forms a stable barrier to oxygen diffusion.
generation.mechanism: The ALD-deposited Al2O3 coating forms an inert, thermodynamically stable oxide scale at high temperature that prevents oxygen from penetrating into the underlying alloy microstructure, thereby preserving its phase stability and associated mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: The coated alloy is expected to show significantly reduced oxygen uptake and minimal oxide scale growth at 1000 °C, while maintaining its baseline room‐temperature ductility (8–16%) and high‐temperature yield strength (163–530 MPa).
generation.baseline: Uncoated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy that undergoes rapid oxidation under high-temperature exposure, leading to degradation in mechanical performance.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective as long as the ALD process produces a uniform, well-adherent coating; however, under extreme thermal cycling or in conditions that may induce coating spallation the protective effect may diminish.
generation.uncertainty: Long-term adhesion of the ALD Al2O3 coating under cyclic thermal-mechanical loading and its resistance to transient thermal shocks are not fully defined and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one set receiving a ~150 nm ALD Al2O3 coating and a control set without coating. Expose both sets to air at 1000 °C for 100 hours. After exposure, perform high-temperature tensile tests under the same strain rate conditions and characterize the oxide scale using SEM/EDS and XRD.
measurements: High-temperature tensile yield strength and ductility
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ALD-coated samples exhibit oxide growth and weight gain comparable to the uncoated samples, or if their high-temperature tensile properties (yield strength and ductility) degrade significantly relative to controls, the hypothesis will be falsified.
